flags.detail: Two different sets of PSS-10 results. 'Study Overview > Results' (source: Results sub-section inside the Review of Literature) says low 8 (17.78%), moderate 35 (77.78%), high 2 (4.44%), SD 6.31, median 21. Table 11, Table 13, Figures 12-13, the Interpretation, Discussion and Summary say low 6 (13.33%), moderate 33 (73.33%), high 6 (13.33%), SD 5.65, median 19 (mean 19.16 in both). Both versions are kept verbatim. The author must confirm which is correct. The Study Overview block looks like it comes from an earlier draft and should be corrected or deleted before publication.

Financial support: Table 10 and Figure 11 show 44 (97.78%) parents/family and 1 (2.22%) scholarship. Three statements say 100%: the Table 10 interpretation ('All 45 (100%) students ...'), the overall socio-demographic findings ('(100%)') and Summary and Conclusion ('for 100% of the students'). The Discussion and Study Overview correctly give 97.78%. Recommended correction: '44 (97.78%)' in all three places, after the author confirms.

AI-chatbot residue in the manuscript: 'This gives you a complete Q1–Q9 Socio-demographic result based on the handwritten data provided.' and, in reference 4, 'Note: Please verify the second author's surname. Your original reference lists “Hasiamson,” ...' (both removed). The text also contains 'the instrument shown in the questionnaire provided for the present study' (reworded) and template phrasing ('the following assumptions can be included'). This means substantial parts of the text, and possibly the data analysis and charts, were produced by an AI assistant from the author's handwritten data. Ask the author for a signed AI-use declaration and for confirmation that every statement, number and reference has been checked (COPE/ICMJE position). Consider publishing an AI-use policy on the website.

The literature review describes studies without citing them, or cites the wrong source: the 2022 systematic review (9,202 participants) is cited as ref 8 (Sharma 2021, a research-methods textbook); the North India cross-sectional study (n = 282, mean PSS 28.67 ± 5.32), the 2021 instrument-development study (430 students) and the 2026 PSS systematic review have no reference at all. The 2023 systematic review and the 2024 umbrella review match refs 7 (Welch 2023) and 1 (Labrague 2024) but are not cited where they are described. Other doubtful placements: ^6^ (Edwards & Burnard 2003, about mental-health nurses) is attached to the author's own study title; ^9^ (Cohen et al. 1983, the PSS paper) is attached to 'research approach' instead of to the PSS description; ^12^ (Basavanthappa, a textbook) is attached to the Table 11 caption; ^1^ (a 2024 umbrella review) supports the definition of stress. The author should supply the missing references and fix the citation numbers.

The manuscript is a converted thesis/proposal. The abstract has no methods or results and says 'I intend to conduct a study'. Background and Delimitations are in the future tense ('The study will be conducted ...'). There are 'Plan for Data Analysis', 'Expected Outcome' and schematic-diagram sections. A second mini-paper (Background/Aim/Objectives/Methodology/Results, now 'Study Overview') repeats the Introduction, Methods and Results. Summary and Conclusion is followed by a separate Conclusion. All of this content was kept, with headings fixed. Recommendation to the author: (1) replace the abstract with a structured abstract (Background, Aim, Methods, Results, Conclusion; <= 250 words) that reports N = 45 and the Table 11/13 results; (2) delete the Study Overview block after reconciling its numbers; (3) turn Plan for Data Analysis and Expected Outcome into a short past-tense 'Statistical analysis' paragraph; (4) merge Summary and Conclusion with Conclusion; (5) put Background and Delimitations in the past tense; (6) consider dropping the schematic diagram or the chart duplicates (see figure flag).

Objective 2 and hypothesis H2 (association between stress and socio-demographic variables) are never tested. The Plan for Data Analysis says chi-square tests 'were used', but no association table, test statistics or p-values are reported. The Overall discussion itself says 'the present frequency and percentage analysis does not establish a statistically significant relationship ... would require inferential statistical tests such as the chi-square test'. H1 ('a significant level of stress') is not testable as written and is not tested. The author should either supply the chi-square results (stress level x each variable, with chi-square, df and p) or remove Objective 2, H1/H2 and the chi-square claim.

In the source, the untitled percentage table under the Figure 2 caption (now Table 12) read Low 13.33% | Moderate 13.33% | High 73.33%, which puts the Moderate and High values in each other's columns. It was corrected to Low 13.33% | Moderate 73.33% | High 13.33% to match Table 11, the pie chart and all text. The table also repeats Table 11 and Figure 13; consider deleting it.

No author affiliation (institution, department, city), e-mail or ORCID. The line under the name, 'Post B.Sc. Nursing', is a qualification or programme, not an affiliation, and was kept as given. A corresponding-author e-mail is needed for the first-page footnote and the website. Ask the author for the full affiliation, e-mail and (optionally) ORCID.

Ethical approval is stated ('Institutional Ethical Committee, Regional College of Nursing, Guwahati') but without an approval number or date. The approval letter and consent form were 'enclosed' in the thesis but not supplied to the journal. Before publication, obtain the approval letter and add the reference number and date to the Ethical considerations section.

The author's surname matches that of the journal's Managing Editor (Dr. Ramavatar Singh Tyagi), who also authors another article in this issue from the same institution (Regional College of Nursing, Guwahati). If the two are related, COPE expects a competing-interest declaration and peer review handled by an independent editor. The paper has no competing-interest, funding, acknowledgement or AI-use declarations.

Methods details that are missing or contradictory: the sampling technique is given as 'total enumeration sampling or convenience sampling' in the text but 'Convenient Sampling' in the schematic diagram; the number of eligible 8th-semester students (response rate) and the data-collection period are not reported; the reliability coefficient 0.79 is given without the method (Cronbach's alpha? test-retest?) or the sample used; and the PSS-10 cut-offs (0–13 / 14–26 / 27–40) are not referenced. Ask the author to clarify.

Inconsistent anonymisation: the title and much of the text say 'a selected nursing institute of Guwahati', but the institution is named (Regional College of Nursing, Guwahati, under SSUHS) in the operational definitions, delimitations, setting, inclusion criteria and ethics. Recommend naming it consistently, or anonymising it everywhere. SSUHS (Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences) is not expanded.

Figure 13 (the author's pie chart, redrawn with its own labels) shows moderate stress as 73.34%, whereas Table 11 and the text give 73.33%. The pie was rounded so that it sums to 100%. Kept as printed in the source chart.

References to verify: ref 8 (Sharma, Nursing research and statistics, 4th ed., Elsevier, 2021) and ref 12 (Basavanthappa, Nursing research, 2nd ed., 2014): check the edition/year pairs. Ref 7 (Welch 2023, J Nurs Educ 62(1), 36–41): check the pages. In ref 4 the author's own draft had 'Hasiamson'; 'Williamson' is correct for Cohen & Williamson (1988). Some sources are old or off-topic (Beck & Srivastava 1991; Edwards & Burnard 2003 is about mental-health nurses, not students).

All 12 source charts (screenshot/WhatsApp exports, 1264–1568 px, with embedded 'Figure n' titles that clashed with the article numbering) were redrawn from the values printed on them. The text-only schematic diagram was redrawn as Figure 1. Original images are kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-international-research-journal/55c29a40-3aee-5b96-9c75-9672107bc1f3/scratchpad/work_p2/orig_figs. Each socio-demographic table is also shown as a bar chart (Figures 2–11 duplicate Tables 1–10, and Figures 12–13 duplicate Tables 11–12), which adds about 6 pages. Most journals ask for either a table or a figure for the same data; consider keeping only the tables.
No received/accepted dates are given in the source (left empty). No data-availability statement.
